`PUMP_TELL_UNDER_FAIRNESS` evaluates every row at the conservative `R_served`. Assumptions: a FAILED `scr_a` still requests its 600 W (the decided default of DA-47, Graph to confirm, OQ-DA-47) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; the battery discharge cap and tier shedding order are `[UNV: Graph]`; A has no reactor, so the batteries only drain: the bus is a clock, not a base. The earlier `b_a1`-only arrangement (540,000 dJ) gives 337 steps = 33.7 s on the full bus, too short for the stall to be read, which is why `b_a2` exists.

### D.17 Reachable-set subject budget

The `subject_budget_per_set` formula is defined as:

`S_int(S) = F(S) + L_seed(S) + C` ; `S_total(S) = S_int(S) + PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE + ACTORS + HORRORS` ; `SUBJECT_BUDGET_SET iff S_int(S) > INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET or S_total(S) > MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` ; `I-7: INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET + PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE <= floor(3 x MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS / 4)` ; `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS_needed = ceil(4 x (INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET + PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE) / 3)`

**Variables:**
| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `F` | int | 0 to 120 | IA D.10 and IA-37; declared interactables (hardpoints, two face subjects per door, valves, hull segments, sockets) | Home 50 (48 + 2 scrubber slots, DA-47), A 28, B 40 |
| `L_seed` | int | 0 to 20 | DA-26 | Seeded loose placements still on the floor: home 2, A 4, B 4 (falls as the player collects) |
| `C` | int | 0 to 18 | IA D.10 | Cap-stub worst case (at most 6 modules x 3 ports), counted once per set |
| `PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE`, `ACTORS`, `HORRORS` (Interaction's `P`, `A`, `H`) | int | 24, 4, 2 | IA D.10, I-7; registry `subject_budget` | 30 together; `H` is `HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX` 2 `[PLACEHOLDER: Horror]` Emitter HORROR subjects (one active plus one transient) |
| `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` | int | 120 `[PLACEHOLDER: Interaction]` | registry (Interaction-owned, IA-37) | Content ceiling for the per-registration-window sum `W_int(p) = F + L_seed + C` at every authored body position, not for `S_int` over a loaded set (registry `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET`, `subject_budget`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* |
| `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` | int | 192 `[PLACEHOLDER: Emitter]` (registry range 128 to 384) | registry (Emitter-owned) | Subject cap |

**Output Range:** `S_int` 70 to 146 and `S_total` 100 to 176 in MVP content as loaded-set sums (the design review's 68 to 144 and 98 to 174 plus the two scrubber slots of DA-47) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
**Example:**

| Set | `F` | `L_seed` | `C` | `S_int` | vs 120 | `S_total` | vs 192 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S0 `{home}` | 50 | 2 | 18 | 70 | pass | 100 | pass |
| S1 `{home, A}` | 78 | 6 | 18 | 102 | pass | 132 | pass |
| S2, S3 `{home, B}` / `{home+B}` | 90 | 6 | 18 | 114 | pass (6 slack) | 144 | pass |
| **S4 `{home+B, A}`** | 118 | 10 | 18 | **146** | **over by 26 as a loaded-set sum (not a registered state, see the D37 paragraph below)** | 176 | pass (16 slack) |

I-7 check: 120 + 24 = 144 = floor(3 x 192 / 4) with `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` 192 `[PLACEHOLDER: Emitter]`, exactly at the limit. Raising the budget to 144 alone breaks I-7 (144 + 24 = 168 > 144) and needs `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` of ceil(4 x 168 / 3) = **224** (a two-owner change, Checkpoint rulings Q4 option 2). The Authoring-only diet (option 3) must remove at least 24 subjects from S4 to bring `S_int` to 120 (the Edge Cases list the named candidates and their readability cost).

**Cumulative table with the instruments and pod consoles that OQ-DA-38 and OQ-DA-39 ask for (design review 2026-10-27).** Instruments are In-World Instruments' indicative placements (home 9, A 4 plus the second battery reading on A that partners `inst_b_a1_stock`, B 5) and the consoles are one per dock room (`airlock`, `a_dock`, `b_dock`); each is an Interaction subject. Neither list is authored yet; this is the arithmetic of adopting both.

| Set | `S_int` as authored | + instruments | + consoles | `S_int` with both | vs 120 | `S_total` (+ 30) | vs 192 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S0 `{home}` | 68 | 9 | 1 | 78 | pass | 108 | pass |
| S1 `{home, A}` | 100 | 14 | 2 | 116 | pass (4 slack) | 146 | pass |
| S2, S3 `{home, B}` / `{home+B}` | 112 | 14 | 2 | 128 | **over by 8** | 158 | pass |
| **S4 `{home+B, A}`** | 144 | 19 | 3 | **166** | **over by 46** | **196** | **over by 4** |

I-7 for a budget of 166: 166 + 24 = 190 and ceil(4 x 190 / 3) = **254**, which leaves `S_total` 196 with 58 spare. The 25-subject diet (S4 144 to 119 as authored) is no longer enough, because it leaves 141 against 120 with both lists placed, and S2 and S3 would breach 120 where the diet never reached. **Intended route:** ASK-I1 (register by body adjacency or proximity, so a far welded section does not spend the budget) or a joint raise to about 166 with `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` about 254; the diet is the last resort, because it removes restorable modules from a game whose pillar is that wrecks have usable organs (P5). S4 reachability is never gated *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.

**User ruling D37 and the registered neighbourhood (2026-10-27).** Interaction registers interactable subjects by body adjacency or proximity and not by "loaded" (ASK-I1 adopted). Define a neighbourhood N as the player's body plus any body adjacent to it; in the MVP a pod-docked derelict is a separate body (BDY-25) and is not adjacent to the home body, and a welded B belongs to the home body `[UNV: Interaction IA-37, the adjacency predicate]`, and the proximity radius is `[PLACEHOLDER: Interaction]`. The gate becomes `SUBJECT_BUDGET_SET iff S_adj(N) = F(N) + L_seed(N) + C > INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET`, with `C` counted once. Worked example with the DA-47 slots: {home} 50 + 2 + 18 = **70**; {A} 28 + 4 + 18 = **50**; {B unwelded} 40 + 4 + 18 = **62**; {home+B} 90 + 6 + 18 = **114**, so the worst case is 114, at most 120 with 6 slack, and S4 `{home+B, A}` (146 as a sum) is never a registered state. With the instruments and consoles of OQ-DA-38 and OQ-DA-39 the neighbourhoods are {home} 70 + 9 + 1 = 80, {A} 50 + 5 + 1 = 56 and {home+B} 114 + 14 + 2 = **130, over by 10**, so the {home+B} rows wait for Interaction's proximity radius and not for a budget raise. The Emitter side is unchanged: `S_total` stays judged on the loaded set, 146 + 30 = 176 of 192 as authored (16 spare) and 168 + 30 = 198 with both lists (6 over), which is one more reason those rows are not authored yet. The I-7 and cumulative arithmetic above is the record of the pre-ruling route and used 68, 100, 112, 112 and 144 (add 2 to each for DA-47) Registry `subject_budget` (Interaction-owned) states the lint as the registration-window form `W_int(p) = F + L_seed + C <= INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` 120 at every authored body position, summed over the registration window plus its one-hop ring (`SUBJECT_WINDOW_HOPS`), with the S4 WARN retired and `P + Y <= PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE` 24 (`Y` the salvage-yield ITEM subjects); where this paragraph says "neighbourhood N" or "adjacency", read that window, and the loaded-set `S_int` formula above is the INFO upper bound only *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.

### D.18 Thermal drift (the cold-room invariant)

The `thermal_drift` formula is defined as (a lint and report formula, harness-side; the natural logarithm is forbidden on the sim path and nothing hashed depends on it):

`tau_steps = floor(100 x V x C_TILE / (K_HULL x S_ext))` = `floor(12000 x V / S_ext)` at the defaults ; `t_cross_min = tau_steps x ln((T0 - T_AMB_MC) / (ONSET_MC - T_AMB_MC)) / 600` for `T0 > ONSET_MC` ; `COLD_ROOM_DRIFT iff t_cross_min < COLD_ROOM_SAFE_MIN` (sealed, unheated, doors closed) ; `COLD_ROOM_UNDECLARED iff T0 <= ONSET_MC and the room is not the declared lethal room`

That pushes me toward trying to minimize the change rather than rework everything, so I'm checking whether there's a way to tighten the scope while still preserving the needed behavior.

I run through alternatives — swapping which fitting is treated as loose, adjusting the demand-side coverage, or excluding one placement from counting toward supply — but none of these feel clean. It's tedious but fully deterministic, so I can hand off a precise mapping table rather than vague instructions.

Removing the placement entirely is the more conservative, mechanically justified edit, so I'll go with that and work out its cascade, while still questioning whether that cascade is strictly required or just tightens the conservative upper bound.
